whatItIs.text: A leaf salad plant grown in hundreds of forms, from crisp iceberg to loose-leaf types; the milky latex in the stem gave it its Latin name lactuca.

historyNote.text: Lettuce was farmed by the ancient Egyptians, who turned an oilseed plant into a leafy crop; the Greeks and Romans took it up — romaine is named for the Roman papal gardens and cos for the Greek island of Kos.

howToChoose.text: Choose heads or leaves that look crisp and brightly coloured with no rust spots or slimy bases; the lighter the weight for its size, the more it has dried out.

storage.text: Wash only when using, and keep leaves dry and loosely wrapped in the fridge.

useItUp.text: Wilted lettuce still works: Blitz into a green soup base, or sear romaine halves cut-side down for a warm salad; the cores regrow in a dish of water.

substitutions.note: tenderer leaves; wilts faster so dress at the table
much more crunch; holds up hot dressings and take-away lunches
